explanations: terra: At the descent, God promises that whoever follows His guidance will neither fear nor grieve, giving one response to the offered path its outcome.

luna: Those who deny the signs are أصحاب النار and abide there; the phrase links the section’s companions of the adverse side to enduring residence. | terra: Those who disbelieve and deny the signs become abiding أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ, matching 90:19 and completing the alternative to 2:38.
terra: A sin that encloses its doer leads to أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ who remain there, a direct adverse counterpart to the section's enduring side-membership.

luna: Those who believe and do good are أصحاب الجنة and abide there; this is the positive counterpart to the Fire companions, supporting the section’s gloss of companions as those who remain attached. | terra: Belief and good deeds lead to أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ who remain there, the paired fortunate company after 2:81.

terra: Righteousness is not turning faces east or west but faith, giving to kin, orphans and the needy, freeing people, and patience; it explicitly relocates moral sidedness from direction to the deeds of 90:13-17.
terra: قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشْدُ مِنَ ٱلْغَىِّ explicitly distinguishes right guidance from error before 2:257 gives the two allegiances their opposed ends.

luna: Believers are brought from darkness into light, while disbelievers are brought from light into darkness and become lasting companions of the Fire; this joins the section’s right-light and adverse-side associations in a distinct paired formulation. | terra: God leads believers from darkness to light, while false powers lead rejecters from light to darkness and make them أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ, a two-course division ending in adhered company.
terra: On judgment day some faces whiten and others blacken, giving the human division two visibly opposed conditions and addressing the rejecters for disbelief.
terra: Those with whitened faces remain in God's mercy, completing the fortunate side of the visible division.
terra: Every soul tastes death, and true success is being drawn away from Fire and admitted to Garden, compressing death and the two final sides into one ayah.

terra: When relatives, orphans, and the needy attend ٱلْقِسْمَةَ, they are to receive provision and kind words; the q-s-m division sense meets the vulnerable people whose care precedes 90's final sorting.

terra: Kindness is commanded toward parents, kin, orphans, the needy, neighbors, traveler, and مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَـٰنُكُمْ; right-hand power is placed under the same mercy ethic that precedes 90's right-hand outcome.
terra: People attribute good fortune to God and misfortune to the messenger, and are told that all is from God, directly correcting human side-like assignments of luck.
terra: Good reaching a person is from God while evil reaching him is from himself, adding moral responsibility to the fortune language of 4:78.
terra: Following a way other than the believers' way after guidance becomes clear ends in Hell, directly joining selected path to final destination.
terra: The prohibition on seeking allotted fortune with divining arrows, تَسْتَقْسِمُوا۟ بِٱلْأَزْلَـٰمِ, joins q-s-m division to attempted fortune and sets a boundary on that practice.

terra: أَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَـٰنِهِم combines q-s-m swearing with aymān as oaths while discussing demanded signs and unbelief, bringing the section's oath, right-root, and signs into one wording.
terra: God commands following His straight path and forbids the multiple paths that scatter people from it, a direct decision-point image for way becoming side.
luna: Iblis says he will sit against people on God’s straight path; this sets up the section’s image of guidance and chosen ways as a contest over direction.

luna: Iblis says he will approach people from before, behind, right, and left; this is a hostile use of side-directions around the guided path, not the final two groups, and continues the preceding threat. | terra: Satan threatens approach from before, behind, عَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ and عَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ; here both sides are avenues of trial, setting a boundary on the final moral labels.
terra: Believers who do good are named أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ and remain there, directly combining company, place, and permanence.
terra: The Garden company recognizes that guidance brought it to its inherited destination, linking the end-place back to the way.

luna: Companions of the Garden call companions of the Fire across their different outcomes; the scene gives the section’s two side-communities a direct exchange. | terra: أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ call to أَصْحَابَ ٱلنَّارِ across their destinations, explicitly staging the two companies as opposed sides.

luna: The condemned are described as blocking God’s path and denying the Hereafter; this makes their road and refusal concrete beside the section’s two guided roads and denied signs. | terra: Those on the adverse side are identified by blocking God's way and seeking to make it crooked, a direct path-to-place relation.

luna: A barrier lies between the Garden and Fire, with people on the heights; this renders the opposing destinations as a spatial boundary. | terra: A barrier stands between the two companies and the people of the Heights recognize both by marks, making their separation a visible spatial order.

luna: Those on the heights look toward the companions of the Fire; this continues the separated groups’ scene from a third position. | terra: When the Heights people's eyes turn toward the Fire's companions, they ask not to be placed with the wrongdoers.

luna: The people on the heights recognize men by their marks and address them; this gives the boundary scene distinct communities and visible affiliation. | terra: The Heights people address men known by their marks, continuing the recognition of the separated companies.

luna: The exchange at the heights turns toward entry into the Garden; this continues the question of who reaches which side. | terra: Those once denied mercy are told to enter the Garden, dramatizing the true allocation against human misjudgment.

luna: Companions of the Fire ask Garden people for water and are refused; the scene makes the boundary and opposed destinations tangible. | terra: The Fire's companions ask the Garden's companions for water or provision, making the opposed sides and their reversed provisions explicit.
terra: The answer explains that denial and treating religion as play barred the Fire's companions from the Garden's provision.

luna: People call good fortune theirs but blame Moses for misfortune; the source section glosses yumn as blessing and شؤم as ill omen, while this ayah shows the ill-omen label being wrongly assigned. | terra: Pharaoh's people claim good as theirs but treat evil as an omen from Moses; the reply locates their طَـٰٓئِرُهُمْ with God, correcting the section's dictionary association of side with good or bad luck.
terra: God separates the corrupt from the good, heaps the corrupt together, and places them in Hell, making moral distinction into grouped destination.
terra: Those who do good become أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ and abide there, joining conduct, fortunate company, and lasting place.
terra: Those who earn evil become أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ and abide there, the adjacent adverse company to 10:26.
terra: Belief, good deeds, and humility lead to أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ who abide there, another direct company fixed to its destination.
terra: مَثَلُ ٱلْفَرِيقَيْنِ compares the two parties as blind/deaf and seeing/hearing, making their difference mutually defining like right and left.

luna: At the coming Day, people divide into wretched and happy (شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ); this echoes the section’s gloss of right as good fortune and left as ill fortune. | terra: On the coming day humanity is divided فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِىٌّۭ وَسَعِيدٌۭ, an exact nonlexical counterpart to ill-fated and fortunate sides.

luna: The wretched are in the Fire with groaning; it completes the adverse half of the division introduced at 11:105. | terra: Those made wretched are placed in the Fire, giving the adverse fortune of 11:105 a destination.

luna: The Fire group remains there for the stated duration; this develops the section’s claim that the final side becomes a place of abiding. | terra: Their abiding in the Fire makes the adverse class's side enduring rather than momentary.

luna: The happy are in the Garden, abiding there; this completes the opposite destination and echoes the section’s fortunate right-side association. | terra: Those made happy abide in the Garden, directly realizing the section's equation of the fortunate side with lasting felicity.

luna: Hell has seven gates and each has an allotted portion (جُزْءٌ مَقْسُومٌ); the section’s q-s-m division of final groups has a specific afterlife parallel here, though this verse describes seven shares rather than two sides.
terra: ٱلْمُقْتَسِمِينَ names the dividers, a direct q-s-m occurrence whose object is specified in 15:91.
terra: Those dividers make the Qur'an عِضِينَ, fragments; this adverse partition of revelation contrasts with the just separation of people according to response to God's signs.
terra: God owns direction to the intended way while some ways deviate, explicitly setting guidance and deviation within the road image.
terra: أَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَـٰنِهِم again combines the two roots in an oath denying resurrection, the event where the two sides are finally disclosed.

luna: Created shadows incline to the right and left while prostrating; this makes right and left tangible as directions, though the ayah describes shadows rather than human moral groups. | terra: Created things cast their shadows عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَٱلشَّمَآئِلِ while prostrating, so both physical sides share submission rather than bearing opposed moral fates.
terra: Everything in the heavens and earth, along with the angels, prostrates to God, completing the scene in which shadows incline on both right and left.

terra: The owners do not make those whom أَيْمَـٰنُهُمْ possess equal partners in provision; it exposes the power and inequality carried by “right hand,” which 90's command to free a neck morally challenges.

luna: Each person’s lot or record is fastened to that person’s neck; the attachment concretely parallels the section’s gloss of أصحاب as those who stay attached to a side, though this ayah does not name either side. | terra: Each person's طَائِرَهُ is fastened to his neck and brought out as an open record, joining fortune or omen, inescapable attachment, and judgment book in one scene.

luna: The person is told to read his record and is his own reckoner; this completes the preceding image of an individual record attached to its bearer. | terra: The person is commanded to read his own record and suffice as his own reckoner, completing the book scene begun by the fastened omen in 17:13.

luna: At the gathering, the person given his book in his right hand reads it and is not wronged; this is another explicit link between the right hand and judgment by one’s record. | terra: People are summoned by their leaders and the one given a record بِيَمِينِهِۦ can read it without injustice, another direct right-hand judgment scene.
terra: The sun's movement ذَاتَ ٱلْيَمِينِ and ذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ makes the two words a literal spatial arrangement around the protected cave.

luna: The sleepers are turned on their right and left sides (ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ وَذَاتَ الشِّمَالِ); this is bodily orientation, not a moral group. It parallels the source section’s dictionary note about the dead being laid on the right, while the verse itself describes sleep. | terra: The sleepers are turned ذَاتَ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ, a bodily right-left scene that continues 18:17.
terra: The truth is announced and belief or disbelief is left as a response, after which a surrounding Fire is prepared for wrongdoers; choice of course becomes place.
terra: Belief and good deeds receive an unlost reward, supplying the fortunate counterpart to the fire scene in 18:29.
terra: God calls Moses مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنِ and draws him near, making the right side a site of divine nearness.
terra: The mindful are gathered to the Merciful as an honored delegation, one collective route toward the fortunate destination.
terra: The criminals are driven thirsty toward Hell, the adjacent opposite procession and destination.
terra: God asks Moses what is فِى يَمِينِكَ, presenting the right hand first as ordinary grasp before 20:69 makes what it holds an instrument of power.
terra: What Moses holds فِى يَمِينِكَ swallows the magicians' craft; the right hand becomes effective power, matching the section's dictionary statement اليمين القوة.
terra: After the sign cast from Moses's right hand defeats the illusion, the magicians fall prostrate and believe, showing that right-hand power serves guidance.
terra: The covenant at جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ is immediately joined to the gift of manna and quails, linking the right side with provision and favor.
terra: God promises that whoever follows His guidance will neither stray nor suffer, turning the offered way into one of two life trajectories.
terra: Turning away from remembrance leads to a constricted life and resurrection blind, giving the rejected course its adverse outcome.
terra: The resurrected person asks why he was raised blind after once seeing, voicing the consequence of his chosen course.
terra: The answer says God's signs came and were forgotten, so he is forgotten that day, closely matching the rejection of signs defining 90's left-hand group.
terra: Excess and unbelief receive recompense, and the afterlife punishment is declared more severe and lasting.
terra: هَـٰذَانِ خَصْمَانِ divides people into two adversarial parties concerning their Lord and begins the Fire-side description.
terra: Believers who do good are admitted to gardens, supplying the other party's destination after the adverse scene begun in 22:19.
terra: Those seeking emancipation from مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَـٰنُكُمْ are to receive a contract and God's wealth, joining the right hand's power/possession sense to 90:13's freeing of a neck.
terra: People أَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَـٰنِهِم that they would obey, but are told not to swear and instead render known obedience, separating oath-language from actual course.
terra: At judgment the wrongdoer wishes he had taken a path with the messenger, directly presenting final regret over a chosen way.
terra: He wishes he had not taken a particular person as intimate friend, identifying companionship as the fork in that path.
terra: The friend led him away from remembrance after it came, explaining how adhered company produced the adverse end.

luna: Thamud say they take an omen from Salih and his followers, and he answers that their omen is with God; the section’s شؤم gloss meets a specific reversal of who bears misfortune. | terra: The people say ٱطَّيَّرْنَا بِكَ to Salih, and he answers that their omen is with God; responsibility replaces their projection of ill fortune onto a messenger.
terra: The call comes from شَاطِئِ ٱلْوَادِ ٱلْأَيْمَنِ in ٱلْبُقْعَةِ ٱلْمُبَارَكَةِ, explicitly joining the right side to blessing, the section's dictionary sense of yumn.

terra: The messenger neither recited a prior book nor wrote one بِيَمِينِكَ; its book-and-right-hand conjunction forms a specific earthly counter-scene to records received in the right hand at judgment.
terra: يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ makes the Hour itself the event in which people are separated.
terra: Believers who did good are made joyful in a garden, specifying one side of the separation announced in 30:14.
terra: Those who disbelieved and denied the signs and afterlife are brought to punishment, specifying the other side in terms matching 90:19.

terra: The parable asks whether those whom your right hands possess are equal partners in provision; it makes right-hand power a social hierarchy rather than an automatic sign of personal blessedness.
terra: أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِنًۭا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقًۭا declares the two moral classes unequal, the conceptual boundary behind their different destinations.
terra: Believers who do good receive gardens as lodging, placing one class in its prepared home.
terra: The defiantly disobedient have the Fire as lodging and are returned whenever they try to leave, making the adverse side lasting.
terra: Two gardens عَن يَمِينٍ وَشِمَالٍ flank Saba's dwelling, and both belong to a blessed provision scene, complicating any automatic equation of physical left with ill fortune.
terra: When Saba turns away, the two gardens on right and left are replaced by bitter, sparse gardens, turning bilateral blessing into loss through response.
terra: The replacement is identified as recompense for ingratitude, showing that fortune attached to the two sides changed through moral choice.

luna: The scripture’s inheritors are divided into three moral classes, from those wronging themselves to those foremost in good; this is another concrete triad beside the section’s cited three classes in 56:7 and its two named sides. | terra: Inheritors of the Book are divided into self-wronging, moderate, and foremost classes, a threefold moral classification comparable to 56:7 rather than a simple binary.
terra: People swear جَهْدَ أَيْمَـٰنِهِم that a warner would make them better guided, yet the warner increases aversion; q-s-m, aymān, and the rejected path meet here.

luna: The town’s people say the messengers are an ill omen for them; this is the accusation that the next ayah reverses, matching the section’s شؤم sense. | terra: The town's people say إِنَّا تَطَيَّرْنَا بِكُمْ and threaten the messengers, staging the human attribution of misfortune which the section associates with shu'm.

luna: The messengers answer that their omen is with them; this completes the reversal and shows ill fortune as an attribution tied to the people’s own conduct. | terra: طَـٰٓئِرُكُم مَّعَكُمْ returns their alleged omen to themselves, turning external bad luck into responsibility for their own excess.
terra: أَصْحَابَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ are joyfully occupied on judgment day, opening a scene of the fortunate company immediately before criminals are separated.
terra: The Garden company and their spouses recline in shade, giving that company a settled place.
terra: Fruit and whatever they request supply the Garden company's provision.
terra: A word of peace from a merciful Lord crowns the fortunate company's scene.
terra: وَٱمْتَـٰزُوا۟ ٱلْيَوْمَ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ commands the criminals to separate themselves that day, explicitly forming the opposite company.

luna: The followers say leaders came to them عَنِ الْيَمِينِ; if this is heard in the source section’s secondary sense of force, it links right with power, though the verse’s phrase is interpretively uncertain and does not name a final side. | terra: The condemned say others used to come عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ; whether “from the right” means the trusted side or forceful approach, it is a significant non-felicitous use of the section's side/strength word.
terra: The leaders answer the accusation about approaching from the right by saying their followers were not believers, beginning the ayah-by-ayah clarification of that phrase.
terra: They deny having authority over the followers and call them transgressors, clarifying that “coming from the right” did not remove the followers' responsibility.
terra: Both parties acknowledge that their Lord's word has fallen due and that they will taste punishment, giving the disputed influence its shared destination.
terra: The leaders admit leading others astray because they themselves were astray, explicitly linking companionship to loss of the way.
terra: Leaders and followers share punishment that day, making their chosen association an enduring adverse company.
terra: Garden inhabitants turn toward one another and ask questions, opening a recollection of a companion who ended on the opposite side.
terra: One Garden inhabitant says he once had a close companion, making personal companionship the hinge of the cross-destination scene.
terra: The former companion had challenged belief in resurrection, voicing the denial that belongs to the adverse course.
terra: He had mocked judgment after death and decay, specifying the belief that separated the two companions.
terra: The Garden speaker asks his company whether they will look, initiating literal sight across the two destinations.
terra: He looks and sees the former companion in the midst of Hell, spatializing the opposed outcomes of their paths.
terra: The Garden speaker says the companion nearly brought him to ruin, naming the causal force of that association.
terra: He credits his Lord's favor for not being among those brought to punishment, locating true good fortune in rescue from the companion's course.
terra: The Garden speaker asks whether they will die again, beginning his recognition that the fortunate destination endures.
terra: He contrasts their first death with freedom from punishment, confirming the permanence of his side.
terra: He names this outcome the great triumph, articulating the felicity attached to his destination.
terra: The call for workers to work toward such an outcome reconnects the final side to action taken before judgment.
terra: Abraham strikes the idols ضَرْبًۢا بِٱلْيَمِينِ; the right hand is the instrument of decisive force and directly realizes the named strength sense.
terra: The verse rejects making believers who do good like corrupters, or the mindful like the wicked, stating the moral boundary behind final separation.

luna: The heavens are folded بِـيَمِينِهِ; the source section’s dictionary form lists yamin as strength, while this verse speaks of divine dominion rather than human right-side groups. | terra: The heavens are مَطْوِيَّاتٌۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦ, using the right hand in a scene of absolute divine power and scale.
terra: The trumpet, death, and resurrection gather all people into the judgment event that culminates in the two processions of 39:71 and 39:73.
terra: The earth shines, the record is set down, and witnesses are brought before judgment, directly preparing the two groups' departure to their destinations.
terra: Every soul is fully repaid for what it did immediately before the two companies are driven toward Hell and Garden.

luna: The disbelievers are driven to Hell in groups; the scene makes a condemned community’s destination a place reached together. | terra: Disbelievers are driven in companies to Hell until its gates open, staging one collective route to an adverse permanent place.

luna: They are told to enter Hell’s gates and abide there; it completes the left-like group’s destination as a lasting place. | terra: The command to enter Hell and abide there closes the disbelieving company's route with permanence.

luna: Those who feared their Lord are driven to the Garden in groups; this sets the opposite community and route beside the Hell-bound group. | terra: Those who feared their Lord are driven in companies to the Garden, the opposite procession and destination to 39:71.

luna: The Garden group says God fulfilled His promise and lets them settle in the Garden; this completes the positive side’s fixed destination. | terra: The Garden company praises God for granting the land to settle wherever it wills, articulating the end-place as an inherited, abiding side.
terra: أَيَّامٍۢ نَّحِسَاتٍۢ names calamitous days in which the wind makes a people taste disgrace, another concrete expression of ill fortune.
terra: The question contrasts one cast into Fire with one arriving secure on judgment day, a concise boundary between the two final outcomes.
terra: فَرِيقٌۭ فِى ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَفَرِيقٌۭ فِى ٱلسَّعِيرِ states the same final spatial division into two enduring companies without right-left vocabulary.

luna: The section identifies the root ق س م with dividing; this verse says God apportioned livelihoods among people (قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ مَعِيشَتَهُمْ). It is a worldly allocation, not the two final sides, so the link is lexical and limited. | terra: نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ uses q-s-m for God's distribution of livelihoods, directly realizing the source dictionary's تقسيم/تفريق sense while distinguishing providential allotment from final moral division.
terra: Whoever turns from the Merciful's remembrance is assigned a satan as an inseparable companion, a concrete adverse form of attachment.
terra: Those companions bar people from the path while the barred people suppose themselves guided, joining companionship directly to a mistaken course.
terra: At the final encounter, the person wishes the distance of the two easts lay between him and his companion, revealing the terrible permanence of the association.
terra: Sharing punishment makes regret useless, turning the attached companionship into common residence on the adverse side.
terra: Those who commit evil suppose they will be made like believers who do good in life and death; the verse condemns that erasure of the two outcomes.
terra: أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ abide there as repayment for deeds, explicitly grounding enduring company in the path already lived.

luna: Two recorders sit on the right and left (عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ); the judgment setting gives the paired directions a role before final group assignment. | terra: The two receivers seated عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ turn right and left into the enduring positions from which a life is recorded.

luna: The next ayah says no word is spoken without a watcher ready; it completes what the two recorders on either side receive, while this ayah itself supplies that paired placement. | terra: Every spoken word has a ready watcher, stating what the right-and-left receivers of 50:17 actually record.
terra: فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَـٰتِ أَمْرًا names those distributing affairs inside an oath sequence, joining both senses developed by the section: oath and apportionment.
terra: تِلْكَ إِذًۭا قِسْمَةٌۭ ضِيزَىٰ condemns an unjust division, establishing a moral boundary around the section's q-s-m image of final separation.
terra: A destructive wind is sent فِى يَوْمِ نَحْسٍۢ مُّسْتَمِرٍّۢ, a Qur'anic scene of an ill-fated day corresponding to the section's shu'm sense.
terra: ٱلْمَآءَ قِسْمَةٌۢ بَيْنَهُمْ uses q-s-m for a regulated division of water, a concrete temporal allotment distinct from the final division of people.

luna: The section cites this three-class staging (أَزْوَاجًا ثَلَاثَةً) before the right and left groups; it makes the paired sides part of a larger reckoning scene. | terra: Judgment makes humanity أَزْوَاجًا ثَلَاثَةً, explicitly turning lived differences into fixed classes; 56:8-10 name those three classes.

luna: The cited أصحاب الميمنة are named here as the people of the right; this is the section’s direct counterpart and positive pole. | terra: The exact designation أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ reappears as one of the judgment-day classes, directly staging the section's right-hand people.

luna: The cited أصحاب المشأمة are named here as the people of the left; this is the section’s direct counterpart and negative pole. | terra: The exact opposing designation أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْـَٔمَةِ makes the left-hand class the spatial and fateful counterpart of 56:8.

luna: After the two side groups, this scene names the third class, السابقون; it preserves the threefold staging that the section quotes at 56:7. | terra: وَٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلسَّابِقُونَ names the third class required by 56:7, preventing the right-left pair from erasing the foremost group in this particular judgment scene.
terra: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ states the distinctive outcome of the third class named in 56:10.
terra: Gardens of delight give the foremost third class named in 56:10-11 its own destination alongside the right- and left-hand classes.
terra: A multitude from earlier peoples belongs to the foremost class, beginning its transhistorical composition.
terra: A smaller number from later peoples completes the composition of the foremost class.
terra: Jeweled couches begin the concrete dwelling of the foremost class, completing the three-class scene introduced in 56:7.
terra: Reclining face to face makes the foremost class a settled company in its destination.
terra: Everlasting youths attending them continues the provision assigned to the foremost class.
terra: Cups and a drink from a flowing spring specify the foremost class's reception.
terra: Their drink causes neither headache nor loss of reason, distinguishing this fortunate provision from harmful drink.
terra: Chosen fruit continues the provision of the foremost class.
terra: Desired bird meat adds to the concrete hospitality of the foremost class.
terra: Wide-eyed companions continue the foremost class's garden scene.
terra: The comparison to hidden pearls describes the companions in that same destination.
terra: The foremost class's provision is explicitly a recompense for what they used to do, tying final place to prior course.
terra: They hear neither vain speech nor sinful talk, distinguishing their lasting company from corrupt association.
terra: Only words of peace are heard, giving the foremost class the greeting later echoed for the right-hand people in 56:91.

luna: أصحاب اليمين restates the right-side group under the hand-name; this is the same community label in the section’s cited scene. | terra: أَصْحَابُ ٱلْيَمِينِ restates the right-hand people with the hand-name which the section identifies as an alternative to meymene.
terra: Thornless lote trees begin the concrete dwelling of the right-hand people named in 56:27 and completed by 56:38.
terra: Layered fruit continues the provision assigned to the right-hand people, making their side a lived felicity.
terra: Extended shade contributes a lasting place of rest to the right-hand group's destination.
terra: Flowing water continues the right-hand people's promised setting and its association with blessing.
terra: Abundant fruit supplies another concrete feature of the right-hand side's provision.
terra: Fruit that is neither cut off nor forbidden makes the right-hand fortune continuous rather than passing.
terra: Raised couches give the right-hand group a settled place, realizing the section's claim that a chosen direction becomes an abiding location.
terra: A renewed creation continues the right-hand people's garden scene and specifies the felicity attached to their class.
terra: The companions' renewed virginity belongs to the same sustained description of the right-hand destination.
terra: Loving, equal-aged companions finish the immediate description before 56:38 assigns it to أَصْحَابِ ٱلْيَمِينِ.
terra: لِّأَصْحَابِ ٱلْيَمِينِ identifies the whole garden description in 56:28-37 as the prepared lot of the right-hand people.
terra: A multitude from earlier peoples is included within the right-hand class, showing that the side gathers a transhistorical company.
terra: A multitude from later peoples completes the temporal breadth of that same right-hand company.

luna: أصحاب الشمال restates the left-side group under the hand-name; this supplies the paired negative label from the same surah. | terra: أَصْحَابُ ٱلشِّمَالِ restates the adverse class with the literal left-hand name and begins its contrasting fate.
terra: Scorching wind and boiling water begin the concrete fate attached to the left-hand people named in 56:41.
terra: The shade of black smoke turns the left-hand side into an adverse dwelling rather than mere direction.
terra: The left-hand shade is neither cool nor pleasant, directly reversing the extended shade of the right-hand scene in 56:30.
terra: Former indulgence explains a lived choice that hardened into membership among the left-hand people.
terra: Persistence in the great sin supplies the moral adherence behind their adverse side, complementing the section's definition of ṣāḥib as one who stays attached.
terra: Their denial that death will be followed by resurrection voices the stance that leads into the left-hand outcome.
terra: Their question about resurrected ancestors completes the disbelief spoken in 56:47.
terra: The command to say that earlier and later peoples will all be gathered answers the left-hand group's denial.
terra: Gathering at a fixed time turns the moral division into an appointed judgment event.
terra: Eating from the tree of zaqqum begins the left-hand group's humiliating reception.
terra: Filling their bellies with zaqqum intensifies the adverse provision assigned to that side.
terra: Drinking boiling water answers the garden's flowing water with the left-hand side's opposite provision.
terra: Drinking like thirsty camels completes that punitive meal scene.
terra: هَـٰذَا نُزُلُهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلدِّينِ names the preceding food and drink as the left-hand group's judgment-day hospitality.

terra: The soul reaching the throat opens the death scene that soon sorts it among the near, the right-hand people, or the denying lost; it also meets the source dictionary's death-and-right-side burial sense.
terra: The witnesses look on as the soul reaches the throat, contributing the human vantage within the death scene that ends in threefold classification.
terra: God is nearer to the dying person than the onlookers although they cannot see, locating the final sorting under unseen divine presence.
terra: The challenge to those who suppose they will not be judged introduces accountability immediately before the soul's class is disclosed.
terra: The demand to return the departing soul if they are truthful establishes death's irreversibility before the three outcomes are named.
terra: The dying person's first possible class is one of those brought near, retaining the threefold division introduced in 56:7-11.
terra: Rest, fragrant provision, and a garden state the outcome of the near class before the right-hand class is named.
terra: At the deathbed classification, being مِنْ أَصْحَابِ ٱلْيَمِينِ makes the right-hand identity the soul's final disclosed station.
terra: سَلَامٌۭ لَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ ٱلْيَمِينِ gives the right-hand class a greeting of peace, supplying the felicity implicit in the section's yumn.
terra: The alternative وَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ introduces the adverse class by its denial and wandering.
terra: Boiling-water hospitality gives that denying class its concrete reception.
terra: Burning in Hell completes the adverse destination opposed to the peace of the right-hand people in 56:91.
terra: The declaration that the preceding division is certain truth seals the three deathbed outcomes as final reality.

luna: The believers’ light runs before them and at their right sides (بِأَيْمَانِهِمْ); the section’s right-side association with a fortunate outcome is made visible as light. | terra: Believers' light running before them and بِأَيْمَانِهِمْ gives the right side visible radiance on the day their destination is announced.

luna: Hypocrites ask to borrow the believers’ light, then a wall separates them with mercy inside and punishment outside; it develops the boundary implicit in the section’s two final sides. | terra: Hypocrites ask believers to share their light, but a wall divides mercy on its inner side from punishment outside, spatializing the final separation.

luna: The separated hypocrites ask believers whether they had not been with them; this continues the partition scene and makes group affiliation part of the division. | terra: The exchange across the wall names self-temptation, waiting, doubt, and false hopes as the path that left the hypocrites without light.

luna: The hypocrites and disbelievers are told their refuge is the Fire; this completes the separation scene with the adverse destination. | terra: No ransom is accepted and the Fire becomes their refuge, making the wall's separation permanent.

luna: Believers have reward and light, while disbelievers who deny the signs are أصحاب الجحيم; the verse joins the section’s right-light association to its denied-signs and fire side. | terra: Believers in God and His messengers have their reward and light, while deniers of signs are companions of Hell; light and the two companies meet in one ayah.
terra: Believers are promised mercy and a light by which to walk, giving the judgment light of the right side an antecedent path function.

luna: The verse says the companions of Fire and Garden are not equal, then calls the Garden companions successful; it directly pairs enduring communities and opposite outcomes. | terra: The verse directly opposes أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ and أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ and declares the Garden's companions successful, exposing ṣāḥib as attachment to a fate.
terra: فَمِنكُمْ كَافِرٌۭ وَمِنكُم مُّؤْمِنٌۭ gives the belief-disbelief division that 90:17-19 turns into the two named sides.
terra: On the Day of Gathering, faith and good action lead to forgiveness and abiding gardens, giving one gathered class its destination.

luna: Those who disbelieve and deny the signs are companions of the Fire, abiding there; this closely restates the section’s denial-of-signs group and supports its gloss of companions as residents attached to a side. | terra: Disbelief and denial of signs lead to أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ, closely matching the definition of 90:19's left-side people.
terra: Believers recall light moving before them and بِأَيْمَانِهِمْ while asking God to perfect it, repeating the luminous right-side scene as prayer.
terra: One walking fallen on his face is contrasted with one walking upright عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍۢ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ, a direct path-image for two ways whose ends cannot be equal.
terra: The question rejects treating those who submit like criminals, another direct refusal to collapse the two human classes.

luna: All are brought into view with nothing concealed; this ayah introduces the public judgment scene before the next ayah assigns the book to the right hand, and it echoes the section’s challenged claim that no one sees. | terra: The universal exposure in which no secret remains hidden sets the judgment scene immediately before records are given on the right or left.

luna: The person handed his book in his right hand introduces the successful side; the section specifically compares this hand assignment with its right-side people. | terra: The record is physically given بِيَمِينِهِۦ, making the right side a disclosed judgment outcome rather than merely a direction.

luna: The right-hand recipient says he expected to meet his account (مُلَاقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ); the section contrasts this correct expectation with 90:5’s false assumption that no one has power over him. | terra: The right-hand recipient says he expected to meet his account, explicitly opposing the mistaken حساب of the human in 90:5 and 90:7.

luna: The right-hand recipient’s pleasant life is the outcome that follows his book and expectation, making the side a lasting destination. | terra: فَهُوَ فِى عِيشَةٍۢ رَّاضِيَةٍۢ turns receipt on the right into a satisfying settled life.

luna: The right-hand recipient is placed in a high garden (جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ); it gives the section’s right-side destination a concrete setting. | terra: A lofty garden supplies the lasting place attached to the right-hand judgment.

luna: The garden’s reachable clusters (قُطُوفُهَا دَانِيَةٌ) continue the right-hand recipient’s scene of settled reward. | terra: Near-hanging fruit specifies the accessible provision of that fortunate side.

luna: The right-hand recipient is told to eat and drink for what he sent ahead; the scene ties his destination to prior deeds, as 90:17 ties the right-side group to faith and compassion. | terra: The invitation to eat and drink for deeds sent ahead ties the right-hand outcome to prior action on the path.

luna: The other person receives his book in his left hand; this is the direct opposite of the right-hand allotment used in the section. | terra: The record given بِشِمَالِهِۦ makes the left side the place of irreversible regret and directly opposes 69:19.

luna: The left-hand recipient wishes he had not received his book, the reverse of the right-hand speaker’s expectation at 69:20. | terra: The left-hand recipient wishes never to have known his account, reversing the confidence of 69:20.

luna: His wish that death had ended matters continues the left-hand recipient’s regret over judgment. | terra: His wish that death had been final shows the irreversible misery disclosed by the left-hand record.

luna: He says his wealth did not avail him; the failed worldly holding contrasts with the final side assigned by his record. | terra: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهْ rejects accumulated wealth as a power able to change the left-hand outcome.

luna: He says his authority has vanished; this continues the left-hand recipient’s loss of worldly standing at judgment. | terra: هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلْطَـٰنِيَهْ declares worldly authority gone, sharply limiting the dictionary association of the right hand with human power.

luna: The command to seize and bind him continues the same left-hand recipient’s transition from regret to punishment. | terra: The order to seize and shackle the left-hand recipient begins the execution of his adverse place.

luna: He is sent into the blazing Fire (الْجَحِيمَ); this gives the condemned side the fire destination that 90:20 names. | terra: Casting him into Hell makes the left-side verdict an actual destination.
terra: Binding him in a long chain makes his attachment to that destination bodily and inescapable.

luna: The punished man did not believe in God; this is a concrete counterpart to the side defined in 90:19 by denying God’s signs. | terra: Failure to believe in God names the first path choice behind the left-hand fate, matching 90:19's disbelief in God's signs.

luna: He did not urge feeding the poor (طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ), reversing the feeding in famine that 90:14, 90:15, and 90:16 places among the acts preceding the right-side group. | terra: Failure to urge feeding the needy directly reverses 90:14-16 and explains why this person receives the left-hand record.
terra: Having no intimate friend that day gives a grim interpersonal counterpoint to aṣḥāb as an enduring company.
terra: The only food being foul discharge continues the left-hand side's reversed provision.
terra: Only sinners eat that food, closing the explanation of who belongs to this adverse company.

luna: The threat says God would seize him بِالْيَمِينِ; the source section lists the dictionary sense yamin as strength, a forceful sense distinct from the blessed right-side title. | terra: لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِٱلْيَمِينِ uses yamin in a seizure of power, a direct Qur'anic setting for the section's secondary definition of right hand as strength.
terra: The rejecters cluster عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ around the messenger, showing that occupying either physical side does not itself make one of the fortunate companions.
terra: Each rejecter clustered on the messenger's right and left hopes to enter a garden, explicitly exposing the difference between physical side and final fortunate side.
terra: The emphatic refusal answers their hope, denying that their physical placement or presumption grants garden membership.
terra: The speakers divide themselves into submitters and deviators, and say the submitters deliberately sought right guidance.
terra: The deviators become fuel for Hell, turning the class distinction of 72:14 into an adverse destination.

luna: Every soul is held to what it earned except the people of the right (أَصْحَابَ الْيَمِينِ); the exception directly establishes the side distinction. | terra: Every soul is pledged for what it earned; 74:39 then marks the right-hand people as the exception, grounding side in deed.

luna: The exception is named أصحاب اليمين, the very right-side community the section links to the coming exchange. | terra: إِلَّآ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْيَمِينِ exempts the right-hand people from the universal pledge for deeds stated in 74:38.

luna: The right-side people are in gardens asking about criminals; this stages the parties whose exchange the section cites. | terra: The right-hand people are فِى جَنَّـٰتٍۢ, giving their class a settled garden location.

luna: The right-side group asks about the criminals; this identifies who speaks across the divide. | terra: They question the criminals from within the gardens, staging communication across the two destinations.

luna: They ask what brought the criminals into Saqar; the question makes the opposite group’s destination explicit. | terra: مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِى سَقَرَ asks what course put the criminals into Saqar, directly joining way taken to final place.

luna: The criminals say they were not among those who prayed; this begins their account of what led to their side. | terra: The criminals first answer that they were not among those who prayed, naming one practice behind their opposing destination.

luna: They say they did not feed the poor (نُطْعِمُ الْمِسْكِينَ), directly reversing 90:14, 90:15, and 90:16’s famine feeding and explaining the section’s use of this exchange. | terra: Their admission that they did not feed the needy directly reverses 90:14-16 and explains exclusion from the right-hand people.

luna: They admit joining those who plunged into vain talk; this gives a concrete account of the company they kept on the condemned side. | terra: Joining vain discourse names the company and conduct in which they remained attached.

luna: They say they denied the Day of Judgment; this directly matches the rejection that marks the section’s adverse group. | terra: Their denial of the Day of Judgment matches the disbelief in signs that defines 90:19's adverse group.

luna: They say certainty came to them; this closes the criminals’ account of reaching the opposite destination. | terra: Certainty arriving ends their denial and fixes the consequence narrated by the whole exchange.
terra: Intercession no longer benefits the criminals, confirming the finality of the course into Saqar explained in 74:42-47.
terra: Some faces are radiant on that day, beginning one embodied judgment class.
terra: Those radiant faces look toward their Lord, specifying the fortunate stance of that class.
terra: Other faces are gloomy on that day, the visible opposite class.
terra: They expect a back-breaking calamity, explaining the ill fortune written on the gloomy faces.

luna: Humanity is guided to a way, then becomes grateful or ungrateful; this directly links the section’s two guided roads with the two kinds of people who reach its sides. | terra: إِنَّا هَدَيْنَـٰهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِرًۭا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا parallels the two guided high roads and immediately divides response into gratitude or disbelief.

luna: For the ungrateful, the next ayah names chains, shackles, and a blaze; this gives the adverse road a concrete punishment. | terra: Chains and a blaze are prepared for the disbelievers, turning one response to the guided way into an adverse end-place.

luna: The righteous are introduced with a drink of camphor; this begins the positive group’s reward scene. | terra: The righteous drink a fragrant cup, beginning the opposite provision for those who took the grateful course.
luna: The righteous fulfill vows and fear a day whose evil spreads widely; this describes the conduct and judgment-awareness of the positive group.
luna: They give food to the needy, orphan, and captive despite wanting it themselves; this is a direct parallel to the section’s feeding of the orphan and poor before the right-side label.
luna: They say they feed only for God, seeking neither repayment nor thanks; this specifies the motive of the compassionate act.
luna: They fear a severe day from their Lord; this continues the good group’s stance toward the judgment that divides the sides.
luna: God protects them from that day’s evil and gives them joy; this supplies the outcome of their stance.
luna: Their patience is rewarded with a Garden and silk; this completes the positive group’s path with a lasting place.
terra: Faces bright on that day give one judgment company a recognizable sign.
terra: Laughter and rejoicing express that company's fortunate state.
terra: Dust-covered faces introduce the opposed judgment company.
terra: Darkness covering those faces deepens the contrast with the bright group.
terra: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْكَفَرَةُ ٱلْفَجَرَةُ identifies the dark-faced group by disbelief and transgression, matching 90:19's defining stance.
terra: The record of the wicked is in Sijjin, assigning one moral class to a named adverse register.
terra: The question about Sijjin emphasizes that the adverse register is a distinct judgment reality.
terra: A written record defines Sijjin's function and links class placement to inscription.
terra: The record of the righteous is in Illiyyin, the opposed register to Sijjin.
terra: The question about Illiyyin formally mirrors 83:8 and marks the paired registers.
terra: A written record defines the righteous register just as 83:9 defines the wicked one.
terra: Those brought near witness the righteous record, linking this register with the third class named in 56:10-11.

luna: The human is described as laboring toward the Lord and meeting Him; this opens the same book-and-destination scene with effort leading to encounter. | terra: Every human labors toward the Lord and will meet Him; the next ayat disclose the two book-reception outcomes of that journey.

luna: The book is given in the right hand; this is another direct hand-assignment of the successful side named in the section. | terra: Receiving the record بِيَمِينِهِۦ identifies the fortunate side at the moment of reckoning.

luna: The right-hand recipient receives an easy reckoning, continuing the reward attached to that hand assignment. | terra: A lenient reckoning is the first consequence of receiving the record on the right.
luna: He returns to his people joyfully; this continues the right-hand scene with a concrete outcome. | terra: Returning joyfully to one's people turns right-hand reception into reunion and felicity.

luna: The other person receives his book behind his back (وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ), a specific reversed placement paired with the right-hand book. | terra: Receiving the record وَرَآءَ ظَهْرِهِۦ is a deliberate alternative staging of the adverse side, contrasted with the right-hand reception in 84:7.

luna: The behind-the-back recipient calls for destruction, continuing the regret of the section’s adverse side. | terra: The behind-the-back recipient calls for destruction, voicing the adverse verdict corresponding to the left side.
luna: He enters the Blaze (سَعِيرًا); this locates the adverse book-receiving group in punishment. | terra: Entering a blaze makes the alternative book-reception an enduring location.

luna: The person later handed his book behind his back had been joyful among his people; this gives the worldly stance that precedes his false expectation in the next ayah. | terra: His former delight among his people supplies the earthly stance behind the adverse end and reverses 84:9's rightful joy.

luna: He thought he would never return to God; this is a specific false expectation opposite the right-hand recipient’s expectation in 69:20 and the section’s mistaken assumption in 90:5. | terra: He supposed he would never return, identifying the false expectation behind his judgment-side placement.

luna: His Lord had been watching him; this completes the false-return scene and answers the section’s 90:7 question about whether anyone sees. | terra: بَلَىٰٓ إِنَّ رَبَّهُۥ كَانَ بِهِۦ بَصِيرًۭا answers that supposition with the divine seeing also stressed in 90:7.
terra: The one who fears receives the reminder, supplying the responsive stance immediately contrasted with the wretched person in 87:11.
terra: The most wretched person avoids the reminder, identifying the stance of the ill-fated class.
terra: That wretched person enters the greatest Fire, turning ill fortune into destination.
terra: In that Fire he neither dies nor lives, making the adverse destination a continuing state.
terra: The one who purifies himself succeeds, providing the fortunate opposite to the wretched person.
terra: Remembering the Lord's name and praying continues the successful person's course after 87:14.
terra: Preferring the nearer life names the competing choice behind the adverse course.
terra: The afterlife is better and more lasting, explaining why preference for the nearer life misjudges fortune.
terra: The human mistakes generous provision for divine honor, exposing an unreliable earthly reading of blessing and fortune.
terra: He mistakes measured provision for humiliation, the opposite error about fortune and allotted share.
terra: The correction begins with failure to honor the orphan, moving the criterion from fortune to the deeds on 90's steep path.
terra: Failure to urge feeding the needy repeats the omission that elsewhere explains the adverse judgment side.
terra: Greedily consuming inheritance continues the conduct exposed after failure to honor the orphan and feed the needy.
terra: Excessive love of wealth completes the earthly value system that mistakes provision for honor and leads toward the adverse judgment.
terra: The oath by the sun begins a chain of paired cosmic images before the soul's two moral possibilities are disclosed.
terra: The moon following the sun supplies the first relational counterpart in that oath chain.
terra: Day revealing the sun begins a light-dark pair within the oath sequence.
terra: Night covering the sun completes the light-dark pair before the soul's division.
terra: The oath by the sky and its builder widens the ordered pairs that precede moral separation.
terra: The oath by the earth and its spread completes the cosmic setup before the proportioned soul and its two impulses.
terra: Within an oath sequence, the soul and the One who proportioned it introduce an interior field that will be morally divided.
terra: The soul is inspired with both its wickedness and its mindfulness, a nonspatial pair of possible courses corresponding to the two high roads.
terra: Purifying the soul succeeds, giving one inspired course its fortunate outcome.
terra: Corrupting the soul fails, completing the opposed outcomes after the oath sequence.
terra: The oath by night as it covers begins the paired cosmic contrasts whose answer is that human striving diverges.
terra: The oath by day as it appears supplies night's opposite before the two human courses are stated.
terra: The oath by the creation of male and female adds another pair immediately before the declaration of divergent striving.
terra: The oath's answer إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ declares human strivings divergent, the same movement from an opening oath toward separated outcomes.

luna: The one who gives and is mindful of God takes the favorable course; this parallels the compassionate good deeds preceding the right-side group. | terra: Giving and being mindful begins the conduct of one of the two divergent courses.
luna: The giver affirms the good; this makes the positive course a matter of belief as well as action. | terra: Affirming the best completes the stance that leads to the fortunate course.

luna: God eases that person toward ease; the chosen course reaches a fitting end, clarifying the section’s road-to-destination image. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ promises facilitation toward ease; the source section's dictionary form yusrā means the left side, so this Qur'anic sense deliberately prevents equating the spelling with ill fortune.

luna: The opposing person withholds and feels self-sufficient; this reverses the generosity and humility associated with the favorable side. | terra: Miserliness and self-sufficiency begin the opposite course and recall the hoarded wealth of 90:6.
luna: That person denies the good; this parallels the denial that defines the section’s adverse group. | terra: Denying the best gives that adverse course the same stance of denial that marks 90:19.

luna: God eases the withholding denier toward hardship; this gives the other course its distinct destination. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ promises facilitation toward hardship, completing the two opposed trajectories.
luna: His wealth will not avail when he falls; this gives a specific limit to worldly possession on the adverse course.
luna: God declares that guidance is His responsibility; this frames the two courses in the preceding and following ayat as guidance.
luna: The first life and the Hereafter belong to God; this completes the guidance frame with the final domain of the two courses.

luna: The surah warns of a blazing Fire; this gives the adverse course a concrete end like the fire over the section’s left-side people. | terra: The warning of a blazing Fire introduces the final outcomes of the two courses described earlier in the surah.
luna: Only the most wretched will burn in that Fire; this identifies the condemned class following the warning. | terra: Only ٱلْأَشْقَى enters the greatest Fire, giving ill fortune its final place.

luna: The condemned person denies and turns away; this concretely matches the rejection associated with the adverse side. | terra: The person who denies and turns away is identified as the wretched one who enters that Fire.

luna: The most God-fearing are kept away from the Fire; this is the positive group’s explicit opposite outcome. | terra: وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا ٱلْأَتْقَى places the mindful person away from that Fire, opposing the ill-fated class.

luna: The God-fearing person gives wealth to purify himself; this links a concrete act of giving to the favorable end. | terra: The mindful person gives wealth to purify himself, echoing the costly ascent before membership among 90's right-hand people.

luna: His giving is not repayment of another’s favor; this specifies the motive behind the positive course. | terra: The giver seeks no repayment of another's favor, clarifying the motive of the conduct that leads away from Fire.
luna: He seeks only his Lord’s countenance; this completes the motive of the giving. | terra: Seeking only the Lord's face completes the fortunate person's stance.
luna: He will be satisfied; this closes the positive course with its promised outcome. | terra: The promise that he will be satisfied gives that course its final felicity.
terra: Disbelievers among the People of the Book and polytheists abide in Hell, the adverse company created by rejection of signs.
terra: Believers who do good are خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ, the explicitly opposed human class.
terra: Their reward is abiding gardens and mutual divine pleasure, giving the believing class its permanent fortunate place.

luna: Those whose scales are heavy receive a favorable outcome; this is a measured division of people into distinct final conditions. | terra: Heavy scales begin a two-outcome judgment based on what was acquired along the way.
luna: The heavy-scaled person is in a pleasing life; this gives the favorable side a lived destination. | terra: A pleasing life is the settled outcome of the heavy-scaled class.
luna: Those whose scales are light face the opposite outcome; the verse marks the other side of the measure. | terra: Light scales introduce the opposite measured class.
luna: The light-scaled person’s destination is the abyss; this names the adverse place. | terra: The abyss becomes that class's destination, turning measured difference into place.
luna: The abyss is identified as a blazing Fire; this completes the measured division with the adverse destination named in the section.
terra: The oath by time opens a compact movement from oath to human separation, structurally paralleling surah 90's opening and close.
terra: Humanity is declared in loss before an exception is made, establishing the adverse side of the division.
terra: Faith, good deeds, and mutual counsel to truth and patience define the exception, closely meeting 90:17's faith and mutual counsel before the right-hand designation.
luna: The surah opens by asking about the one who denies the Judgment; this is the denial that the section associates with the adverse side.
luna: That denier repels the orphan; this gives another concrete reversal of the care that precedes the right-side label in 90.
luna: He does not urge feeding the poor (طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ), matching the section’s specific link between the condemned group and failure to feed.
